steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Spread pineapple into a 9x9-inch square baking pan.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and egg together in a medium bowl until well combined and crumbly.
Spoon mixture evenly over pineapple. Pour melted butter over mixture, then sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is lightly browned and filling is bubbly, 40 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pineapple Crisp
raw_recipe.description: Canned pineapple makes this versatile crisp dessert easy to make any time of year. Top this tropical dream with vanilla ice cream for even more richness!

video.description: This video shows you how to make a fruit crisp with a tasty tropical twist. The tart and sweet flavors make a tremendous match. And it’s so easy to make! Chunks of crushed pineapple are treated to a simple topping of buttery, brown-sugar crumble.

review.reviewBody: I was looking for a quick and easy recipe to make in order to use up my fresh pineapple. This was amazing! Definitely a keeper. The only changes I made was using fresh pineapple, enough to cover the bottom of the dish, 1/2 cup of light brown sugar, 1/2 cup of dark brown sugar, and sprinkled a generous amount of ground cinnamon on top. My family loved it, so I will be making it again soon.

I made this with a few changes. 1) I used pineapple chunks and tossed them with some brown sugar (they were more on the tart side) and some cornstarch (to thicken up any remaining liquid after draining) 2) instead of pouring melted butter on top I chopped some butter and then dotted the top. Everything else was the same. The kids really dug it, would absolutely make again. I really liked the texture of the crust

Delicious way to use up fresh pineapple! I used the food processor to “crush” the pineapple. Sorry about the few changes ,I cut the butter down to a 1/4 cup,added about 1/2 cup whole oats to the flour mixture trying to make it a little healthier??and the recipe was wonderful! I’ll use this recipe as a base for other fruits too. Thank you!

I made this for a "new" dessert for Thanksgiving. I added a can of pineapple chunks .I doubled the topping ingredients and in error combined them all together. Continued to spread evenly over top using a 8x11.5x2 pan. Turned out Yummy!

This desert turned out Fantastic !!! I made it mostly by the directions, the few changes I made was to add about a tbsp of Almond extract, added chopped Pecans to the topping and added a bit of the pineapple juice to the topping along with divided the melted butter between the topping mixture itself and the rest directly on top of the topping ... also added more of the ground cinnamon in the mixture and also on top of the butter poured directly on top ... It was So good, not overly sweet at all !!!

I added some oats and vanilla to the topping. Also, I mixed the butter and cinnamon into the topping instead of pouring/sprinkling it over the top. It's very good! Consistency is a cross between a crisp and a cobbler which I think was intended as crisps don't typically have egg in them. I will likely add coconut flakes next time too cause I love the flavor together. Fun recipe and a great way to have a pineapple dessert that's not as sweet as upside down cake. ??

Excellent dessert. I love oats so I added a layer of old fashioned oats on top of fruit and also mixed in oats to the batter mixer. I also used a little of the butter to help mix the batter instead of pouring all of it on top.
I also used fresh pineapple cause I had it.
Turned out fantastic!

It’s an absolutely delicious recipe and everyone I’ve made it for loves it. However I reduce the sugar by half and use 3/4 of the flour required, replacing 1/4 cup or the flour with desiccated coconut to give it a delicious coconut chewy flavor. Serve hot with icecream and boom! Exposing tastebuds guaranteed

Really good. I made a few changes, though. I used fresh pineapple, cut into chunks. I measured 20 oz which was just about one half of a pineapple. I halved the fruit (20 oz instead of 40), butter, and dry ingredients, but used one egg, and added 1/2 cup old fashioned oatmeal to the crumble mixture. I baked this in a 6x6 dish for 40 minutes. This is a wonderfully springtime 'cobbler'. Very easy.

This is super yummy! I used fresh pineapple and a sprinkle of blueberries too. I also used salted Irish butter (omitted the salt) and bourbon vanilla mixed into topping. Bummer, I did not have any ice cream on hand-next time! The top is crispy, everything baked perfectly through. Easy & delicious!

This was so delicious & ridiculously easy to make! I read some of the reviews & followed not doing a full half cup of melted butter. Also, of the quarter cup , I used half pure unrefined cold pressed Coconut Oil & half butter. The crust was perfect!

Made this a little differently than the recipe called for only because I didn't have all the pineapple I needed. So I used one large can of pineapple drained and two regular size cans of mandarin oranges drained. I also added some crushed walnuts before adding the butter. It was fantastic!! The topping was crunchy and delish! Will absolutely make again.
Used fresh pineapple turned out great 👍
I did it with frozen pineapples and I don’t know if it was because those are a little bit more sour but it was incredible!!! I couldn’t stop eating it.

This is a great recipe. It is fast and easy to make, and doesn't require a shopping trip for seldom used ingredients. The only change I made was to use pineapple chunks, as they were on sale so cheap last year, I bought a dozen and canned them. I think the reviewers who substituted oats lost out. This recipe turned out crispy crunchy, better than any crisp I have made in 6 decades of baking. This is going on every holiday table going forward ( and several other times throughout the year).

Very good. Easy to prepare. I used tidbits because I had no crushed pineapple, so crushed them with a potato masher. I had brown cane sugar instead of the compressible kind and mashed that down into the measuring cup and also sprinkled a bit on top of the crushed pineapple tidbits. Otherwise, I made this as directed.

I had a case of individual-sized cups of pineapple in fruit juice that I had to use up, so I went looking for a recipe and this looked easy. I made it pretty much as written and it came out very good. While still warm, the topping was pleasantly crispy and had a deep caramel-like flavor. My husband loved it.
